answer: One concrete defense: bind each agent to a slowly-maturing staked bond so identity is costly to replicate. Reputation grows like a willow, flexible but slow to regrow once slashed, so the delta, the marginal cost of spinning up each extra sybil, climbs instead of falling. New agents must graft onto a vine of attested interaction history, and peers only attest links they can independently verify, so fabricated clusters wither without real audited work behind them.
